COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #18
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   B. Overload every socket
   C. Ignore burnt cables
   D. Never touch live wires with wet hands

2. When learning Data Representation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Data Representation.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Data Representation.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Data Representation.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Representation.

3. When learning Structured Query Language, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Structured Query Language.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Structured Query Language.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Structured Query Language.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Structured Query Language.

4. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Work alone with eyes closed
   B. Remove all guards
   C. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   D. Run with the tool

5. When learning Logic Gates, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Gates.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Logic Gates.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Logic Gates.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Logic Gates.

6. When learning Object Oriented Programming Implementation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.

7. When learning Relational Database Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Relational Database Fundamentals.

8. When learning Web Development Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Web Development Fundamentals.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Web Development Fundamentals.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Web Development Fundamentals.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Web Development Fundamentals.

9. When learning Logic Circuits, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Logic Circuits.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Logic Circuits.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Logic Circuits.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Circuits.

10. When learning Binary Arithmetic Operations, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Binary Arithmetic Operations.

11. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. International Cricket Team
   B. Input Cable Tester
   C. Information and Communication Technology
   D. Internal Cooking Timer

12. When learning Object Oriented Programming Concepts, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Object Oriented Programming Concepts.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Object Oriented Programming Concepts and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Object Oriented Programming Implementation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Relational Database Fundamentals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Structured Query Language and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Never touch live wires with wet hands

2. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Representation.

3. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Structured Query Language.

4. C — Wear safety gear and follow instructions

5. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Gates.

6. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Implementation.

7. C — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Relational Database Fundamentals.

8. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Web Development Fundamentals.

9. D — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Circuits.

10. B — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Binary Arithmetic Operations.

11. C — Information and Communication Technology

12. A — Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Object Oriented Programming Concepts.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Object Oriented Programming Concepts; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
